author: Vieillot, 1819
habitat: 간척지, 도랑가·물웅덩이 부근의 마른 땅(둥지 자리)

months.note: 봄에는 3월 말~5월, 가을에는 8월 말~10월에 드물게 나타나며, 국내에서 기록된 달이다.

summary: 우리나라에서는 보기 드문 철새이거나 길을 잃고 찾아오는 새이다. 작은 무리를 짓거나 민물도요 무리에 섞여 간척지에 내려앉아 먹이를 찾으며, 혼자 또는 암수가 함께 먹이를 찾을 때가 많다. 유폐목 연체동물과 딱정벌레·벌·파리·메뚜기 무리의 곤충을 즐겨 먹는다. 북극 연안 툰드라에 분포해 작은 도랑가나 물이 고인 곳 근처의 마른 땅에 접시 모양 둥지를 틀고 알 4개를 낳으며, 한국·일본·오스트레일리아·아프리카·남아메리카·쿠릴 열도 등에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Pectoral Sandpiper (Calidris melanotos), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean reclaimed land on spring passage in May: crown blackish-brown streaked and fringed rufous, forming a dark cap; a whitish supercilium; lores and ear coverts pale rusty-white with fine dark streaks; neck and breast densely streaked dark brown on a buff-grey ground, the streaked bib ending in a sharp, straight line against the white belly; mantle and scapulars blackish with rufous and buff fringes; flanks and belly clean white; central tail feathers black; bill blackish-brown with a paler olive-yellow base, slightly drooping; legs dull greenish-yellow.
art.pose: foraging on damp ground of reclaimed land, side view
art.scene: Korean reclaimed land on spring migration in May, damp ground with shallow pools and short green grass; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view standing: dark rufous-fringed cap, whitish supercilium, finely streaked pale face, dense dark streaks on neck and breast ending in a sharp line against the white belly, dark-centred rufous-fringed back, slightly drooping blackish-brown bill, greenish-yellow legs
juvenile (autumn), side view standing: brighter rufous cap, neat white lines along the mantle edges, buff breast finely streaked and sharply cut off from the white belly
adult, in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in line: black central tail feathers forming a dark centre to rump and tail, white sides to the rump, grey-brown outer tail, faint wing-bar
art.build: Medium-sized sandpiper, about 22cm, a little larger than Dunlin, with a small head on a rather long neck; males noticeably bigger than females. Bill about as long as the head, slightly drooping towards the tip. Legs medium length, dull greenish-yellow. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a faint narrow wing-bar and a black centre to the rump and tail with white sides to the rump. Walks steadily through short grass and wet ground, often upright and alert.
avoid: Do not let the breast streaks spread down the flanks as chevrons or fade out gradually; that is Sharp-tailed Sandpiper (Calidris acuminata).
Do not give it a bold white eye-ring and bright orange cap; those also suit Sharp-tailed Sandpiper.
Do not paint black legs or an all-black bill; the legs are greenish-yellow and the bill base pale.
Do not draw a long, strongly curved bill or a black belly patch (Dunlin).
